newsitem.title: UK: IPE crude, gas oil firm more on N.Sea, APIs.
newsitem.headline: IPE crude, gas oil firm more on N.Sea, APIs.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures nudged firmer on Wednesday, building on modest earlier gains on North Sea supply and disruption and Tuesday's U.S. stock data, brokers said.
By 1140 GMT , front month September Brent was six cents higher at $18.28 a barrel, with gas oil $1.25 firmer at $164.25 a tonne, though both were trading in low volume.

Brokers said American Petroleum Institute (API) data after Tuesday's market close, which showed higher-than-expected crude stocks for the week ending July 18, as well as a North sea pipe closure had helped lift the market.
"We've seen buying interest in the U.S., and the APIs was also gave the market a lift." one broker said. "A pipe closure in the North Sea may also have contributed."
Production at the North Sea Nelson oil field was shut down on Wednesday until at least Friday due a minor technical problem.
Brokers also pointed to a firmer Sept/Oct spread as an indication of slightly more positive sentiment on the physical market, where physical Brent traded on Tuesday at August +10 cts.
GNI Research on Wednesday pegged strong resistance just below $18.50 per barrel, while it placed support at $18.00.
The API said gasoline stocks fell by 2.79 million barrels to 197.8 million despite both high output and imports.
London brokers said both crude and gas oil were likely to continue to trade in narrow ranges until further news on the resumption of Iraqi crude exports transpires.
"No-one wants to trade while Iraq is up in the air. We're in a very narrow trading range. The volumes say it all, " a broker said.
A U.N. spokesman on Tuesday said the approval of Iraq's aid distribution plan, which Iraq insists on before it resumes exports, was not expected until the end of July.
Iraq needs to sell around 1.5 million barrels of crude per day in order to raise the $1 billion it needs to buy humanitarian aid before the current phase of the deal ends in September.
The second phase of the oil-deal started on June 8.
